texts: During cold aerobic arrest with blood cardioplegia, the oxygen that reaches the myocardium depends mostly on the oxygen dissolved in the cardioplegia.
Hypothermia shifts the oxygen dissociation curve to the left, so haemoglobin holds its oxygen tightly and releases little to the cold heart.
Dissolved oxygen, which rises with a high oxygen tension and is more soluble in cold fluid, is free to diffuse into the arrested muscle.
A rightward shift, the haematocrit and the delivery pressure matter less than this dissolved fraction.
In the picture, the red doughnuts clutch their bubbles in the cold while the free silver bubbles drift onto the stopped fans.
Memory hook: in the cold, the free bubbles feed the fans.
